result.summary: PASS. Причина устранена в обоих местах (запись в store.js и чтение в depsOf): файл результата хранится и отдаётся байт в байт, а файл с настоящим секретом не принимается; поправка правила заглушек (слова your и example считаются заглушкой только для значения из латинских букв, цифр, _, . и -) работает: все 126 образцов отказа отклоняются, все 120 образцов «хранится» хранятся, а склеенный с секретом текст вроде &redirect=https://example.com теперь отклоняется. Моя проверка на 53 тысячах склеенных форм и на 3,3 млн случайных строк не нашла ни одной формы, которую старый код скрывал бы, а новый хранит, кроме принятых владельцем остаточных рисков (4), (6), (7); красных тестов ровно двенадцать по замыслу, правила журнала не тронуты, подгонки под образцы нет. Остались только три Низких замечания, они не блокируют.

findings.what: The try/catch around findSecrets in depsOf catches every error, while the comment above it says the cause is the RangeError of the key-prefix regular expressions on a run longer than about 5.3 MiB. A different error (a bug inside findSecrets) would be turned into the fixed withheld line for every file, with no trace and no signal; the effect is fail-closed and visible to the reviewer of the task (the file is not handed over), so no secret leaks, but a defect of the check would hide itself. Measured: a hand-placed 6 MiB file gives the withheld line and no exception, as designed.
findings.fix: Optional: catch only RangeError (`catch (err) { if (!(err instanceof RangeError)) throw err; return FILE_WITHHELD; }`) so that any other error still reaches closeAfterError, or say in the comment that every error is meant to be fail-closed. No change of the behaviour measured above.

findings.place: tools/src/pixel-office/mask.js:317-328 (the contract comment of findSecrets) and :838-843 (FIND_PREFIXED)
findings.what: findSecrets throws RangeError (look-behind regular expressions with an unbounded repeat) on a single key-shaped run longer than about 5.3 MiB (measured: 6 MiB throws, exactly 5 MiB does not, for the four prefixed rules). The dependence on the 5 MiB limit of result files, which keeps store #publish and acceptResult step 1 from ever reaching it, is written only in runner.js above withheldOrContent; the function that can throw says nothing. If FILE_BYTES_MAX is raised later, the two write-side callers get an exception from a place that looks pure.
findings.fix: Add one sentence to the header comment of findSecrets (callers hold the input to FILE_BYTES_MAX; above about 5.3 MiB the prefixed-key rules throw RangeError), or bound the repeat (a bound of a few thousand characters is enough to decide the form). No change of the behaviour measured.

findings.place: tools/README.md:253 (residual risks of findSecrets) with tools/src/pixel-office/mask.js:996-1027 (findNamedValue resumes after the end of a value)
findings.what: Differential run against an independent reference written from the requirement text (patched only for the amended class Z): 69 of 2.4 million random strings (four seeds) plus 7 of 200 thousand differ, always in one direction (reference refuses, code keeps), never the other. All of them are one shape: the end of a kept value is itself a name word and is followed directly by a quote and a colon (a path, a bare identifier or a placeholder word that is also a key name, then the next pair glued on), or the glued pair sits inside a kept call value. The second kind is residual risk (7); the first kind is the same cause (the pass resumes after the end of the value, as design 2.2 says) but is not named in the README sentence of (7), and the old rules hid such text. Realistic probability is very low (it is not valid JSON), so it blocks nothing.
findings.fix: Optional: widen the README words of risk (7) ("not scanned inside") to say that a name that stands as the end of a kept value, with a quote and a colon glued behind it, is not read as the next pair; or accept as is. ORCH decides whether it is worth a defect (see issues I3).

issues.text: Facts of the task checked: six files in the change; 548 tests, 536 green and exactly twelve red by design, named and counted from my own run; the removed-lines search in mask.js is empty; 120 keep and 126 refuse with no mismatch. Nothing contradicts the task. The expected verdict was not in the task; the verdict comes from my own reading (AP-018).

Pass 1 remarks are all closed in the current code: SECURITY F1 (class Z, measured above), F2 and F4 (README), F3 (depsOf withholds), REVIEWER F1 (comment on the copies of isLineEnd and QUOTES, present above findIsWs) and F2 (distinct names). The rework stayed inside the list of remarks (AP-019): the six files only, the extra function withheldOrContent is the remedy of SECURITY F3. For TEST-DESIGNER (check especially): the 17 C26 and 12 O26 records and the pairs 'starts with your / contains example' for a value inside and outside the character set in all three places; O25 and C25 (counting of trailing closers); a clean file beside a refused one (not accepted, source stays), the same text in the event, the question of the team and the error line, a repeated name listed once; a depsOf trial above 5.3 MiB (withheld, no exception) and a file of an older core; BOM and CRLF bytes on the three inputs; the README greps with the three new words; linear time on the 12 families and on glued example chunks.

Question to ORCH (Low, no block): finding F3 is a shape not named among the residual risks (a kept value that ends in a name word with a quote and a colon glued behind). It is outside the current requirement and run; if ORCH wants it closed or named, it is a small defect for a later run together with the README words of risk (7). Findings F1 and F2 are optional hygiene of the same kind and can go to the same defect.

Not a finding: a differential count on the sources of Sai itself shows the price of the rule: two source files of tools/src would be refused if an agent wrote them (mask.js because of the PEM rule words, language.js because of a message text after the name secret). This is the named price of the rule (README, 'false refusal') accepted by the owner in decisions/0102; recorded so that the report to the owner can say it in plain words.
